task: Task 2 round-1 fix: OnceLock cache + placeholder arm + negative-path tests
summary: All three round-2 changes are clean from a security perspective. The OnceLock cache contains only compile-time static data with no per-tenant contamination risk. The placeholder arm for request_public_write_confirmation is correctly gated behind the existing JWT requirement on tools/call. The two new negative-path tests correctly exercise the error paths anonymously and confirm the typed -32602 envelope shape. One informational note carried forward.

round1_findings_status.SA-T2-01: OPEN (not addressed in round 2 — dev artifact 'Consumed by Task 4's handler' in tools/list description still present in tool_definitions(); SA-T2-01 is a pre-ship cleanup item, not a blocker). New placeholder arm error string also references 'agent-native-distribution Task 4' but this is only reachable by authenticated callers so impact is lower.
round1_findings_status.SA-T2-02: OPEN (no per-field length cap added — acknowledged as non-blocker, bounded by MAX_PEEK_BODY globally).
round1_findings_status.SA-T2-03: CARRIED FORWARD as advisory for Task 4. Not actionable in Task 2.

round2_changes_reviewed.analysis: The cached value is computed entirely from (1) tool_definitions() — a pure static JSON literal — and (2) skill manifest constants baked at compile time via include_str!. No request-time input, no per-tenant data, no network call touches the cache value. OnceLock::get_or_init guarantees exactly-once initialization under concurrent access per Rust's memory model — no data race, no TOCTOU. The cache is a process-level singleton shared by all requests, but because the content is exclusively public tool definitions, there is zero cross-tenant contamination risk. The previous per-request Vec<Value> allocation was not a security issue; the cache is purely a performance improvement.

The arm returns a static string error with no user input echoed and no storage access. It is only reachable after passing the bearer_auth_middleware JWT gate (tools/call is not in ALLOWLIST_METHODS). The error message references 'agent-native-distribution Task 4' — an internal artifact — but since this path requires a valid JWT, the information is exposed only to authenticated callers, which is a significantly lower risk than SA-T2-01 (anonymous-accessible tools/list description). Still worth cleaning up before v1 tag for the same reason as SA-T2-01, but classified INFO not LOW given the auth gate.
round2_changes_reviewed.note: Using -32601 (MethodNotFound) for 'handler not yet implemented' is a mild semantic stretch — the method is tools/call; the tool name is what lacks a handler. The existing catch-all uses -32603 ('unknown tool') which is more precise. This is a code-reviewer concern, not a security issue. No action needed from security perspective.

round2_changes_reviewed.analysis: prompts_get_unknown_name_returns_invalid_params: sends 'mnemonik-does-not-exist' anonymously, asserts HTTP 200 + JSON-RPC error code -32602 + data.field='name' + data.received='mnemonik-does-not-exist'. This correctly verifies the echo behavior and confirms no secret or server-internal data is present in the error response. resources_read_bad_uri_scheme_returns_invalid_params: sends 'https://invalid-scheme/foo.md' anonymously, asserts same -32602 envelope shape. Both tests exercise the anonymous error path without a Bearer token, confirming these branches are accessible pre-auth (correct for discovery methods) and return only typed, non-sensitive error data.

open_findings.action: No action in Task 2. Task 4 must add explicit Claims=Some guard before HMAC computation in request_public_write_confirmation handler.

overall_assessment: Task 2 implementation is security-sound. The two open findings (SA-T2-01, SA-T2-02) are pre-ship cleanup items, not blockers. SA-T2-03 is carried forward as an advisory for Task 4. No new security issues introduced in round 2.
